title: Flaky Rust test: bounded_coordination_mqtt_subscriber_persists_peer_claim_overlay fails intermittently in CI
description: rust/src/gossip.rs test gossip::tests::bounded_coordination_mqtt_subscriber_persists_peer_claim_overlay intermittently panics at src/gossip.rs:2560 with 'local claim publishes only after subscription' (published == false). Observed on the develop->main promotion PR run at 57b5e770 (2026-10-16 09:30 UTC) and on PR #404 at 32094d35 (2026-10-16 16:37 UTC, docs-only change), while the same code passed at f9d047ac (15:49 UTC). Likely cause: collect_coordination_gossip_window_with uses a 500 ms window, and on a loaded CI runner the SUBACK-gated publish (dedicated publish thread, see 231e9a75) can land after the window closes. Fix so the test is deterministic (synchronize on the publish rather than a wall-clock window, or make the window bounded by an event plus a generous ceiling) without weakening the 'publish only after subscription' assertion. Every PR's rust job can go red on this, so it blocks merges.

comments.author: home
comments.text: PR #405. Root cause was a test-isolation race, not the window: KANBUS_REALTIME_BROKER is process-wide, so concurrent router tests connected to this test's mock broker, which took the first CONNECT as its publisher, relayed the foreign claim and exited; the real publish then found no listener and returned false. Fix (test-only): after SUBACK the mock serves every connection and keeps only the router:issue:kbs-peer claim; window ceiling 500 ms -> 1500 ms. Repro with router tests: 6/6 failed before, 0/20 after; full gossip set under 8-way load 0/100. Gates: fmt, clippy, cargo test --lib (553) green locally.

Awaiting Ryan's ACCEPT to merge.
